title: Tenant Observability & Evidence Contract for Regulated VPC Deploys
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines the observability, telemetry, and evidence requirements Redwood expects for regulated customers deploying the Private (VPC) product. It is an operational contract that outlines the metrics, traces, logs, retention, and artifacts required for customer acceptance, ongoing compliance, and post-incident audits.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a concrete, testable checklist that field engineers, SREs, and customer infra teams can use during private VPC deployments to satisfy regulatory evidence requests (PCI/ISO/SOC-style) and internal Redwood SLAs.
- Scope: Applies to all Private VPC deployments for customers with regulated workloads (PHI, PCI, PII-sensitive). This covers control-plane connectivity, runtime agents, telemetry pipelines, and secure artifact handoff.

Key objectives:
1) Ensure visibility to support 99.95% tenant-facing availability SLO and latency SLOs (see SLOs section).
2) Collect and preserve evidence for security and compliance audits with tamper-evident retention controls.
3) Standardize acceptance tests and artifacts to reduce delivery time and avoid rework.

SLOs and performance thresholds (tenant-facing):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for tenant inference endpoint (measurement: synthetic probes from customer region + control-plane logs).
- Latency: p95 < 120ms for 256-token synchronous calls; p95 < 250ms for 1024-token calls (measured at ingress for successful 2xx responses).
- Error budget: 0.05% of requests may return 5xx or timeouts; any breach requires incident runbook and customer notification within 1 hour.

Observability categories and minimums:
1) Metrics (Prometheus-format):
   - Required metrics exported by runtime-agent and control-plane: redwood.runtime.requests_total, redwood.runtime.requests_failures_total, redwood.runtime.latency_seconds_bucket (histogram), redwood.runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio, redwood.controlplane.sync_latency_seconds, redwood.controlplane.config_version{tenant}, redwood.controlplane.fallback_count.
   - Scrape frequency: 15s for runtime-agent critical metrics, 60s for control-plane aggregated metrics.
   - Retention: raw metrics retained in customer-visible TSDB for 90 days; aggregated rollups (1h) for 2 years.

2) Traces (OpenTelemetry):
   - Required spans: request ingress, runtime decode/encode, model kernel exec, kv-cache lookup, control-plane routing decision.
   - Sampling: adaptive sampling with minimum 5% global sample and 100% sampling for any request flagged as failed (>5xx) or taking >p99 latency.
   - Retention: traces retained for 90 days in a tamper-evident store (customer-managed or agreed third-party like Tempo+S3 with signed manifests).

3) Logs (structured JSON):
   - Required logs: access logs (per-request), runtime-agent system logs, control-plane audit logs, key rotations, and storage access attempts.
   - Format: JSON with at minimum {timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, route, model, status_code, latency_ms, node_id}.
   - Retention: 365 days for audit logs; 90 days for operational logs unless regulatory requirement dictates more.

4) Telemetry integrity and chain-of-custody:
   - All telemetry bundles delivered for audits must include salted hashes (SHA256) and a signed manifest from the control-plane operator.
   - For air-gapped customers, manifests must be exportable via signed tarball and verified with customer-provided key.

Evidence artifacts (deliverables for acceptance and compliance):
- Live SLO dashboard link (Grafana) scoped to tenant with view-only credentials.
- A 30-day extract of: metrics (Prometheus export), traces (OTLP export), and logs (JSON NDJSON) for the agreed window.
- Signed telemetry manifest and hash list (SHA256) with timestamped signatures.
- Configuration snapshot: control-plane config_version, model versions, container images with image digests, and quantization/precision profile.
- Access & audit log slice showing KMS/HSM key uses during install and initial 7 days.

Acceptance tests and checklist (field delivery):
1) Pre-install (customer infra):
   - Validate VPC CIDR and routing per network readiness checklist.
   - Confirm KMS/HSM integration and that customer can accept signed manifests.
2) Installation validation (engineer run):
   - Synthetic probe checklist: 5 probes from each customer region to runtime SNI endpoint. All probes must return 200 within latency SLO for initial acceptance.
   - Metrics ingestion validation: Verify runtime-agent metrics scraped at 15s and visible in Grafana panels.
   - Traces: Generate 100 synthetic requests with varied sizes; confirm 5% sampled traces + all failures sampled; spans contain model and kv-cache annotations.
   - Logs: Export last 24 hours of structured logs and validate JSON schema and presence of required fields.
3) Compliance artifact handoff:
   - Produce the signed telemetry manifest and initial 30-day artifact bundle (or since-boot) and deliver via agreed channel (secure S3, signed USB for air-gap).

Example telemetry ingestion config (YAML snippet for runtime-agent):
telemetry:
  metrics_scrape_interval: 15s
  otlp_endpoint: https://collector.customer-vpc.example:4317
  trace_sampling:
    default_rate: 0.05
    spike_capture_threshold_ms: 1500
  log_format: json
  log_shipper: fluent-bit

Evidence export command examples:
- Metrics (Prometheus TSDB block export): curl -u readonly:token "https://prom.customer-vpc.example/api/v1/export?range=30d" -o metrics-30d.tar.gz
- Traces (OTLP export): otelcli export --endpoint https://collector.customer-vpc.example:4317 --from=2025-09-01 --to=2025-10-01 --out traces-30d.ndjson

Operational runbook pointers (post-acceptance):
- Alerting: Must configure the following alerts at customer and Redwood side: runtime_errors_rate > 0.5% for 5m; p95_latency > 140ms for 10m; telemetry_pipeline_lag > 2m for 5m.
- Incident evidence protocol: When an incident is created for a regulated tenant, the on-call engineer must capture: 1) A zipped telemetry bundle (metrics + traces + logs) covering incident window +/- 60 minutes. 2) Signed manifest and chain-of-custody note stored in customer evidence bucket. 3) Post-incident RCA attached with references to artifact hashes.

Upgrade & rollback evidence expectations:
- For any runtime upgrade affecting model execution (kernel/quantization changes), the delivery packet must include: pre-upgrade baseline metrics/traces (7 days), smoke test results, and canary traffic plan; post-upgrade artifact bundle (first 24 hours) and a signed rollback-ready image digest list.
- Rollback procedure must preserve telemetry artifacts from the failed upgrade window and mark them immutable for the duration of the investigation.

Acceptance signoff template (required fields):
- Tenant ID: 
- Deployment ID: 
- Control-plane config_version: 
- SLO verification: pass/fail with measured values
- Evidence artifacts delivered: list of file paths and manifest hash
- Signatures: Field engineer / Customer security lead / Redwood delivery lead (email + timestamp)

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: Private Deployments Delivery - delivery-oncall@redwood.ai
- Observability owner: Eng Platform Metrics team - metrics@redwood.ai
- Escalation matrix: see /confluence/eng-oncall/incident-process (must be mirrored into customer handoff docs).

Security and privacy notes:
- Telemetry exports MUST be filtered for tenant PII unless customer explicitly requests full payload capture and provides documented legal approval.
- KMS keys used to sign manifests must be rotated per customer policy; Redwood will provide rotation proof (signed key rotation log) as part of audit artifacts.

FAQ (short):
Q: What if a customer cannot host a Prometheus/OTLP endpoint?
A: Redwood can host a collector in a dedicated ingress VPC peered to the customer per the hybrid-control-plane model; in that case additional network ACLs and data residency controls are required and documented in the network appendix.

References and related docs:
- Private deploy acceptance and smoke validation (linked), post-install telemetry checklist (linked), and control-plane manifest format specification (internal doc).

Appendix A - Minimal evidence table (human readable):
Artifact | Minimum window | Format | Retention | Delivery method
Metrics export | 30 days | Prometheus TSDB / csv | 90 days raw, 2y rollups | secure S3 / scp
Traces | 30 days | OTLP -> ndjson | 90 days | signed tarball / s3
Audit logs (KMS/Install) | 365 days | JSON NDJSON | 365 days | s3 w/ bucket policy

Appendix B - Contact matrix and escalation SLA:
- Tier 1 response: Delivery engineer within 1 hour
- Tier 2 escalation: Platform SRE within 4 hours
- Tier 3 legal/compliance engagement: within 24 hours
